acceptance_scope: Task workflow regression after public routing description changes; not AI coverage of every tool.

get_celestial_pos.description:
Calculate the altitude and azimuth angles of a celestial object.

Use when: you need one named object's position at a specified place and instant.
Do not use when: you need an all-night target list or a complete observing decision.
Requires: object name, observer coordinates, observation time, and its IANA timezone.
Follow-up: get_celestial_rise_set for events; get_nightly_forecast for night targets;
    plan_stargazing_session for a complete observing decision.

Args:
    celestial_object: Name of object (e.g. "sun", "moon", "andromeda")
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Observation time string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains "altitude" and "azimuth" (degrees).

get_celestial_rise_set.description:
Calculate the rise and set times of a celestial object.

Use when: you need one object's rise/set events. Choose calendar_day for the local
    date containing time, or next_events for the next rise and next set after time.
Do not use when: you need a continuous observing window or a complete night plan.
Requires: object name, observer coordinates, time, timezone, and the intended event scope.
Follow-up: get_celestial_pos for position; plan_stargazing_session for observing windows.

Args:
    celestial_object: Name of object (e.g. "sun", "moon", "andromeda")
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Date string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string
    event_scope: "calendar_day" (default) finds the events in the local calendar
        day containing ``time``. "next_events" finds the next rise and next set
        independently, rolling into following days when needed.

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains "rise_time" and "set_time".

get_moon_info.description:
Get detailed information about the Moon's phase and position.

Use when: you need lunar phase or illumination facts, with optional observer-local events.
Do not use when: you need to rank observing sites or assess a target's overall suitability.
Requires: time and timezone; supply both lat and lon for local position and rise/set.
Follow-up: get_telescope_targets for equipment-aware targets; plan_stargazing_session
    for the combined effect of moonlight, weather, place, and observing goals.

When ``lat`` and ``lon`` are provided, also returns the Moon's local
altitude, azimuth, moonrise, and moonset relative to the observer.

Args:
    time: Date string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees (optional, for local position)
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees (optional, for local position)

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains illumination, phase_name,
    age_days, elongation, earth_distance, and optionally altitude/azimuth
    plus moonrise/moonset (UTC unix timestamps).

list_visible_planets.description:
Get a list of solar system planets currently visible (above horizon).

Use when: you need planets above the observer's horizon at a specified instant.
Do not use when: you need all-night visibility, darkness guarantees, or equipment ranking.
Requires: observer coordinates, time, and timezone; above-horizon visibility alone
    does not establish dark-sky or telescope observing conditions.
Follow-up: get_celestial_pos or get_celestial_rise_set for a selected planet;
    plan_stargazing_session for a planetary observing decision.

Args:
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Observation time string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" is a list of planet dicts (name, altitude, azimuth).

get_constellation.description:
Get the position (altitude/azimuth) of the center of a constellation.

Use when: you need a named constellation's center position at a place and instant.
Do not use when: you need to identify which constellation contains arbitrary coordinates,
    or to choose individual observing targets.
Requires: constellation name, observer coordinates, time, and timezone.
Follow-up: get_nightly_forecast for individual night targets; plan_stargazing_session
    for a complete observing decision.

Args:
    constellation_name: Name of constellation (e.g. "Orion", "Ursa Major")
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Observation time string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains name, altitude, azimuth.

get_nightly_forecast.description:
Get a curated list of best objects to view for the night.

Use when: place and night are known and you need general night targets and a night window.
Do not use when: you need telescope-specific target matching or regional site selection.
Requires: observer coordinates, time within the intended night, timezone, and optional limit.
Follow-up: get_telescope_targets for known optics; get_shooting_plan for an imaging schedule;
    plan_stargazing_session when place or night still needs comparison.

Args:
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Date string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (Time of observation, or just date)
    time_zone: IANA timezone string
    limit: Max number of deep-sky objects to return (default 20)

Returns:
    Standard envelope; data contains:
    - moon_phase: Moon details
    - planets: List of visible planets
    - deep_sky: Sorted list of deep sky objects (Messier/NGC)
    - night_window: Civil-dark window for the requested night

get_tool_catalog.description:
Get metadata for all registered MCP tools.

Use when: you need the wrapped catalog with full documentation and parameter summaries.
Do not use when: your client only needs standard MCP tools/list discovery or a business result.
Requires: no inputs; this call discovers tools and does not perform observing analysis.
Follow-up: choose a tool from its use/do-not-use guidance; plan_stargazing_session
    is the primary entry for complete observing decisions.

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data.tools" contains tool metadata objects.

light_pollution_map.description:
Get light pollution data for a specific area.

Use when: you need a bounding-box grid of light pollution measurements for a map or analysis.
Do not use when: you need ranked places or a complete observing decision.
Requires: south/west/north/east bounds and optional grid zoom.
Returns: data.grid points with brightness, Bortle class, and SQM, plus bounds and zoom.
Follow-up: analysis_area for synchronous place candidates; submit_area_analysis
    for background place analysis; plan_stargazing_session for an observing decision.

Returns a grid of light pollution data points including brightness, Bortle class, and SQM.

Args:
    south, west, north, east: Bounding box coordinates.
    zoom: Grid resolution zoom level (default: 10). Higher = more detailed.

analysis_area.description:
Analyze a geographic area for suitable stargazing locations.

Use when: you need synchronous place candidates or cached pages for a fixed regional query.
Do not use when: the search needs background polling/cancellation or a complete night plan.
Requires: south/west/north/east bounds; keep search parameters fixed while changing pages.
Follow-up: analysis_area with the same query for other pages; submit_area_analysis
    for background work; plan_stargazing_session for dates, weather, and target decisions.

This tool searches for dark, accessible locations with good viewing conditions.
Results are cached based on search parameters.

**Fast mode**: Set ``road_radius_km=0`` to skip road connectivity checks.
This avoids OSMnx network downloads from Overpass API and is much faster —
use it when you only need candidate locations with light pollution and
elevation data, without road distance analysis.

Args:
    south, west, north, east: Bounding box coordinates.
    max_locations: Maximum number of candidate locations to find (before pagination).
    min_height_diff: Minimum elevation difference for prominence.
    road_radius_km: Search radius for road access. Set to 0 to skip road checks.
    network_type: Type of road network ('drive', 'walk', etc.).
    avoid_popular_spots: Penalize heuristically popular locations when ranking results.
    prefer_quiet_at_night: Favor locations that are likelier to quiet down at night.
    popularity_radius_km: Preference horizon for the popularity heuristics.
    db_config_path: Optional path to database config.
    page: Page number (1-based).
    page_size: Number of results per page.

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains:
    - items: List of location results for the current page.
    - total: Total number of locations found.
    - page: Current page number.
    - page_size: Current page size.
    - resource_id: Cache key for the non-pagination search parameters.

submit_area_analysis.description:
Submit bounded background place analysis and return its task identifier.

Use when: a geographic place search may outlive one tool call and needs background control.
Do not use when: you need a complete observing decision or only want to poll an existing task.
Requires: request.bounds and optional place-search preferences;
    max_locations must be from 1 to 100.
Returns: task snapshot with task_id, resource_id, state, and normalized request.
    Active duplicate queries share a task. Completed retries may use cached data.
Follow-up: get_area_analysis_task to poll; get_area_analysis_result after success;
    cancel_area_analysis_task if no longer needed; plan_stargazing_session for decisions.

get_area_analysis_task.description:
Poll an area task's state, deadline, failure, and normalized request.

Use when: you have a task_id and need execution state, failure, or remaining physical work.
Do not use when: you need result pages; do not submit a new job merely to poll.
Requires: task_id returned by submit_area_analysis in the same server runtime.
Returns: task snapshot with state, failure, request, and execution_pending. Running progress
    is unknown; success does not guarantee the separate result cache still exists.
Follow-up: get_area_analysis_result after success; cancel_area_analysis_task if unwanted.
    On TASK_RUNTIME_CHANGED, resubmit the original request rather than polling the old ID.

cancel_area_analysis_task.description:
Logically cancel queued/running area work and discard its late results.

Use when: a submitted area task is no longer needed and its late result must not publish.
Do not use when: you want to delete cached data or interrupt another domain's operation.
Requires: task_id returned by submit_area_analysis in the same server runtime.
Returns: idempotent cancellation snapshot; an existing terminal state stays unchanged.
    A running provider call keeps its execution slot until it actually finishes.
Follow-up: get_area_analysis_task to confirm state and execution_pending;
    wait for physical work to drain before considering resubmission.

get_area_analysis_result.description:
Page a successful area task's existing cached result without recomputing.

Use when: get_area_analysis_task reports succeeded and you need its original result pages.
Do not use when: the task is queued/running and you only need to poll its state.
Requires: the successful task_id, page >= 1, and page_size >= 1.
Returns: cached items, pagination metadata, and resource_id with the task's publication
    version checked; this call never silently recomputes missing data.
Follow-up: get_area_analysis_result with the same task_id for other pages;
    get_area_analysis_task for state; resubmit the normalized request on TASK_RESULT_EXPIRED.

get_telescope_targets.description:
Recommend astrophotography targets for a telescope setup.

Use when: place, time, and optics are known and you need ranked deep-sky imaging targets.
Do not use when: you only need naked-eye targets, a timed schedule, or a choice of sites.
Requires: focal length, observer coordinates, time, and timezone; supply known sensor
    and optical details for matching. For equipment presets use plan_stargazing_session.
Follow-up: get_shooting_plan for timed imaging slots; plan_stargazing_session
    if the observing place or night still needs comparison.

Given a telescope/camera configuration and observing location+time,
returns a ranked list of deep-sky objects best suited for imaging.

Args:
    focal_length_mm: Telescope focal length in mm (e.g. 250 for RedCat51)
    lon: Observer longitude in degrees
    lat: Observer latitude in degrees
    time: Observation time string "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    time_zone: IANA timezone string (e.g. "Asia/Shanghai", "UTC")
    aperture_mm: Telescope aperture in mm (optional, for limiting magnitude)
    sensor_width_mm: Camera sensor width in mm (optional)
    sensor_height_mm: Camera sensor height in mm (optional)
    sensor_pixel_size_um: Camera pixel size in microns (optional)
    central_obstruction_pct: Central obstruction percentage (0-50)
    reducer_factor: Focal reducer factor (default 1.0)
    barlow_factor: Barlow/extender factor (default 1.0)
    mount_type: "equatorial" or "altaz" (default "equatorial")
    filter_type: Filter type — "Hα", "OIII", "SII", or None for LRGB
    limit: Maximum number of targets to return (default 20)

Returns:
    data.targets[] — ranked list, best first.  Each target has:
        name, type, magnitude, catalog
        altitude, azimuth, dawn_altitude
        angular_size_arcmin, angular_size_min_arcmin, angular_size_pa_deg
        surface_brightness (mag/arcmin²), fov_fit_score, fov_fill_ratio
        suitability_score (0-100), mosaic_recommended, optimal_rotation_deg
        rise_time, set_time, transit_time, transit_alt (UTC unix timestamps)
        altitude_curve[{time, alt}]
        civil_dusk, civil_dawn, observation_time
    data.moon — {illumination, phase, altitude_curve, always_down,
        always_up, dark_fraction, moonrise, moonset}
    data.config — the TelescopeConfig used
    data.total — number of targets returned

get_shooting_plan.description:
Generate a single-night astrophotography shooting plan.

Use when: optics, place, and night are fixed and you need matched targets in timed slots.
Do not use when: you still need to choose a site or compare nights, or only need target ranks.
Requires: focal length, observer coordinates, time, and the observing timezone
    (defaults to UTC); optional sensor, optical, and minimum-altitude settings.
Follow-up: get_telescope_targets for target details; plan_stargazing_session
    to reconsider place, date, equipment preset, or observing constraints.

Runs match_telescope_targets then generate_shooting_schedule,
returning targets + moon + timed shooting slots in one response.

Returns:
    data.targets[] — same structure as get_telescope_targets
    data.moon — {illumination, phase, moonrise, moonset,
        always_down, always_up, dark_fraction, altitude_curve}
    data.plan — {date, slots[{start_time, end_time, target_name}],
        total_exposure_min, moon_phase, moon_illumination, moon_delay_min}
    data.config — the TelescopeConfig used
    data.total — number of matched targets

get_weather_by_name.description:
通过地点名称获取综合天气（当前 + 小时预报 + 日预报）。

Use when: you have a place name and need weather facts for that resolved location.
Do not use when: you already have exact coordinates or need a complete observing decision.
Requires: an unambiguous place name; use full administrative names for Chinese locations.
    Provider selection can remain at the server's default aggregation policy.
Follow-up: get_weather_by_position for precise coordinates; plan_stargazing_session
    to combine weather with darkness, targets, and alternative observing sites.

Geocoding uses offline China gazetteer (CJK) → Photon → Nominatim cascade.
Weather data is aggregated from multiple providers with graceful
fallback — open-meteo is always available without an API key.

**中文地名提示**：建议使用完整行政区划名称，如 "浙江安吉"、"杭州西湖区"。
内置离线行政区划数据会正确解析到对应的行政区（如安吉县），而非 POI 商铺。
需要精确定位时优先使用 ``get_weather_by_position(lat, lon)``。

Args:
    place_name: 地点名称。中文请使用完整行政区划（如 "浙江省安吉县"），避免仅用2-3字短名。
    provider: provider 模式，可选 all/qweather/open-meteo/wttr。

Returns:
    Dict，包含 keys: "data", "_meta"（成功时）或 "error", "_meta"（失败时）。

get_weather_by_position.description:
通过经纬度获取综合天气（当前 + 小时预报 + 日预报）。

Use when: you have precise coordinates and need current and forecast weather facts.
Do not use when: you only have a place name or need ranked observing sites or night targets.
Requires: latitude and longitude; provider selection can remain at the default policy.
Follow-up: get_weather_by_name for place-name input; plan_stargazing_session
    to compare observing places and nights using weather and other evidence.

Weather data is aggregated from multiple providers with graceful
fallback — open-meteo is always available without an API key.

Args:
    lat: 纬度
    lon: 经度
    provider: provider 模式，可选 all/qweather/open-meteo/wttr。

Returns:
    Dict，包含 keys: "data", "_meta"（成功时）或 "error", "_meta"（失败时）。

get_best_stargazing_plan.description:
Create a composite stargazing plan for a region and time.

Use when: an existing bbox-first integration needs ranked regional places for one night.
Do not use when: starting a new intent-based integration, providing a place name,
    comparing several nights, or only requesting weather facts.
Requires: south/west/north/east bounds, observation time, and timezone.
Returns: data.query, ranked data.candidates with scores, windows, weather and targets,
    and data.summary; all within the standard response envelope.
Follow-up: plan_stargazing_session is preferred for new integrations;
    get_multiday_stargazing_plan preserves bbox-first comparison across nights.

get_multiday_stargazing_plan.description:
Compare one to seven consecutive nights and recommend the best night and place.

Use when: an existing bbox-first integration compares one to seven consecutive nights.
Do not use when: starting a new intent-based integration, querying nonconsecutive dates,
    more than seven nights, or checking background task status.
Requires: south/west/north/east bounds, local start_date, timezone, and optional night count.
Returns: normalized data.query, per-night plans, the best night, and summary;
    each night uses its own civil-dark window.
Follow-up: plan_stargazing_session is preferred for new integrations;
    get_best_stargazing_plan for the compatible single-night regional detail.

plan_stargazing_session.description:
Preferred end-to-end planning entry point for choosing when, where, and what to observe across one to seven nights.

Use when: you need a complete observing decision or comparisons of places and nights.
Do not use when: you only need raw weather, celestial facts, or task status.
Requires: request.location (place name, center/radius, or exact bounds) and start_date; timezone, one-to-seven nights, observing goal, equipment preset/overrides, and constraints have explicit defaults or are optional.
Returns: normalized request, decision, alternatives, evidence, uncertainties, missing inputs, ranking-change conditions, and next actions in the standard envelope.
Follow-up: get_shooting_plan for an imaging schedule at the selected place/night; get_weather_by_position for updated weather facts. Inspect missing inputs and next actions before treating a degraded decision as final.

get_local_datetime_info.description:
Retrieve the current datetime and timezone.

Use when: you need the server environment's current time and local timezone.
Do not use when: you need time at a remote observing site or already have its timezone.
Requires: no inputs; local means the server environment, not the user's observing site.
Follow-up: use the observing site's explicit time_zone in celestial and
    plan_stargazing_session requests; do not infer it from the server timezone.

Returns:
    Dict with keys "data", "_meta". "data" contains "current_time" (ISO string).
